items.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I always wanted to play a shuffle with Ray Brown. It’s like I love Ray Brown.

ctx.x: Let me ask you the question about you’re on a desert island and you can take five CDs or LPs.

Okay. Well see I’ll tell you that in a second. But what I was going to tell you, I’m sorry I got off my track with the not hiring women and stuff. But now like with Diva and Five Play, I don’t know if it’s the people, because I work with them all the time anyway, but like our bass player, I used to have this incredible fantasy. I always wanted to play a shuffle with Ray Brown. It’s like I love Ray Brown. But now I mean I love playing with Nicki. I think she’s one of the best bass players I know. And now it just…
Only five? That’s not enough. Well this has really been a fascinating conversation. I wish you all the best in the future.

items.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: And he did a duo record with Ray Brown and he’s very much in the style of Ray.

ctx.x: Yeah. I’m actually negotiating with a fellow in France who admires our project here and he says would you let me try to do some interviews with French musicians, and he’ll send them to me, etcetera. So there are things that are happening that may not have happened.

Hey, Monk, there’s a — I did a tour with a great pianist named Oliver Jones, and the bass player on the gig was a French man named Pierre Boussaguet. I think he lives in Toulouse. And he did a duo record with Ray Brown and he’s very much in the style of Ray. He’s a great musician. He would be — if you’re looking for any Frenchmen, he swings his brains out. He’s great.
Great. I may ask you to spell that name out for me.
